_about: Chassis. Not classes: any silhouette, any component in any slot. Numbers are in tens. armour is taken off every blow that lands on bare hull, flat, so small hits bounce off a heavy machine (a standing shield blocks a blow whole; nothing bleeds through). recharge_field is shield regained each battlefield phase spent out of combat; in a fight shield comes only from components (never a free refill, so withdrawing is not a reset). cooling is heat shed at the start of every skirmish turn (0 if absent): venting is a tactic, but a round of ballistics or shields is a way of cooling too. hardpoints is the number of free slots (and of hp_<n> pins on the model); fixed lists the components built into the chassis (always on the die, never removed, no hardpoint used); loadout is the components fitted to the hardpoints by default, and a hardpoint left empty is an entry on the die that does nothing. Every component is one entry, so die size is fixed count plus hardpoints. passive is zero or one object: name and description are shown (the codex prints NAME: description), effects are what the engine runs, at most three, one idea (an upside and its cost count as one passive); the validator refuses effects the engine cannot execute. Shown to the player: codex (the inspect entry, combat and hangar), flavour (an in-world quote), the passive's name and description. design is internal and never shown: fantasy (pitch, inspiration, homages), niche (the role it is meant to fill). Makers are placeholders.

makers.name: Minerva Heavy Works
makers.style: Armour first. Everything is a tank, even the ones with legs.
makers.voice: Maintenance manual. Terse, exact, proud of tolerances.

makers.name: Kestrel Dynamics
makers.style: Fast, fragile, over-tuned. Airframes and interceptors.

makers.name: Wainwright & Sutler
makers.style: Quads and artillery. Old firm, odd designs, everything works.

makers.name: Aphelion
makers.style: Descended from the deep-space programme, back since before the rifts opened. Humanoid frames, hover platforms, variable geometry; high-tech suites over light hulls. White with a pearl sheen, red markings.

makers.name: The Arsenal
makers.style: The Council's own R&D house, which need not compete for favour. Heavy walkers, plasma and energy that runs hot and never crits, big single hits, execute, burn. Dark steel and gunmetal, black chrome.

entries.name: Honey Badger

design.fantasy: A repurposed mining vehicle, designed to take severe punishment and keep on working. Refurbishments were minimal, basically bolting on weapons and armour, it keeps most of its utilitarian mining machinery flavour.
design.name_clash: Flagged 28 September: the id badger is Heavy Gear's Badger APC and BattleTech's Badger transport; the nickname Honey Badger is nobody's. Kept: the shown name is clear.

entries.codex: The Minerva EX-45L (colloquially nicknamed the "Badger") was popular a mining mech widely praised for its reliability and durability, being designed to operate in the harshest, deepest environments imaginable. Reports exist of Badgers being caught in cave-ins while mining over 5 kilometers underground, only to dig their way out to the surface by nightfall, just in time for drinks with the crew. So naturally, when the Rifts opened, the ever-practical Minerva engineering team's first instinct was to finally give their prized Badger claws, teeth, and as many missiles as it could carry, putting its legendary longevity to work on the battlefield.

passive.name: Reinforced Skeleton
passive.description: Legendary Minervan strength. Components can be cracked but never destroyed. Melee attacks deal +10% damage. Cracked weapons become melee-typed, instead of their usual type.

entries.flavour: Hey Russ, ain't that yer Badger over there, covered in demon innards? I thought they retired the ol' girl!

entries.name: Clydesdale

design.fantasy: A massive, boxy, heavily armoured, and utilitarian quadruped walker, designed to fill whatever niche the squad is lacking. Like its namesake, it has four thick legs and carries a massive payload on top.

entries.codex: Surprisingly, or perhaps not, the ever-pragmatic Wainwright & Sutler were the first surviving manufacturer to field a combat walker when the invasion first began. Not knowing the full scope of the threat, the Clydesdale was positioned as a rugged and effective jack-of-all trades, a true workhorse befitting its namesake. A hundred years later, and the original design is still barely changed, its signature W&S simplicity being favourited by pilots and maintenence crews alike. It also serves as an effective training vehicle, as its notoriously poor turning radius results in one less thing for a green pilot to worry about on the battlefield.
entries.flavour: Pilot manual footnotes: Most of the Clydesdale controls are just for show. The only ones you really need are accelerate and alpha strike.

entries.name: Sparrowhawk

design.fantasy: A priority-target interceptor. Designed for speed and firepower and not much else, taking out a key asset and fleeing while its generous shields recharge.
design.name_clash: Flagged 28 September: Sparrowhawk is a Halo UNSC gunship and a BattleTech aerospace fighter, and ours is an aircraft too. Kept for now so the build stays green; Ryan to rename or confirm.

entries.codex: Shortly into the invasion, it was determined that the masses of zombies, demons, and otherwordly things were, frankly, quite dumb without a guiding intelligence coordinating them. Naturally, Kestrel won the bid to produce a small interceptor aircraft, designed to eliminate priority targets and disengage before getting overwhelmed. However, the weapons package traditionally mounted on such a small frame proved ineffective to the task. It wasn't until one inspired engineer suggested cutting all 'uneccesary' weight from the design that a breakthrough was achieved; Armour, weapon regulators, ejection systems, and padded seats were all deemed frivolous, and their omission skyrocketed the Sparrowhawk to excel in its role.

passive.name: Disabled Weapon Regulators
passive.description: Premium Kestrel "feature." Double damage and double heat for all weapons.

entries.flavour: There's lighting a fire under your ass, and then there's piloting a Sparrowhawk. I suggest a cold plunge before you strap in.

entries.name: Mandrill

design.fantasy: A long-armed, stubby-legged plantigrade walker with a high tech suite of weapons and equipment mounted on its backpack. Not fast or heavily armoured, it specializes in battlefield control through status effects and high-tech equipment with complex effects.
design.notes: Numbers, loadout, passive and designation are Claude's first fill (26 September) for Ryan to tweak: hull under the Clydesdale's, shield and field recharge a touch above, a big heat budget for an energy kit, walker legs at 2. The kit is Aphelion's own control suite (two Umbra Projectors to suppress, a Solar Flare Array to burn, a Corona Shield that cleanses, a Pulse Repeater for tempo) plus a borrowed Heat Sink. The passive turns a status on the target into damage.
design.name_clash: Flagged 28 September: Mandrill is a BattleTech 'Mech (a 50-ton Clan Fire Mandrill design) and a Clan name, and Ryan says it looks like ours. Kept only so the build stays green; the Drill (the mandrill's cousin) is Claude's suggested rename.

entries.codex: Looking like a cross between an orangutan and a troll, what the Mandrill lacks in speed or endurance it more than makes up for with high-tech Aphelion technomagic. After the rifts first opened (and upended everything mankind knew about the laws of physics and the nature of the universe), Aphelion set to work assimilating the torrent of new data, developing experimental countermeasures at a frenetic pace. One unlucky researcher managed to knock out his past self using a localized pocket paradoxical time loop. The effect was quickly weaponized and a frame built to lug the heavy device in into battle, nicknamed the "Mandrill" in the researcher's memory.

passive.name: Subspace Solenoid
passive.description: Reads an affliction as a field and drives the shot along it. Attacks deal +50% damage to a foe carrying any status.

design.fantasy: A squat, heavily armoured walker with short, thick legs, its back bristling with weaponry from shielded ports that can seal for additional protection. The cockpit is tucked under the front armour, providing reduced visibility but extra protection. An internal electric generator shocks foes that strike is hull when activated.
design.notes: Probably needs taunt effects on one or more locked or stock components. Wants a retaliate ability that  damages and/or causes status on foes that hit hull, but not sure if that is a passive or component that needs activating. Landed from the content editor 28 September: numbers, fixed component and loadout are the Mandrill's (the editor's template shape), the designation is Claude's fill in Minerva's register, the sixth hardpoint takes Minerva's Ablative Plating because a shipped chassis fills every slot, and the passive is planned until the engine can run it. All Ryan's to move.

passive.name: Weapon Shielding
passive.description: Threshold for component damage is greatly increased.

design.fantasy: An unstoppable assault tank, complete with front rams and plows, designed for breaching reinforced emplacements - or plowing over and through fodder monsters.
design.notes: Passive should be something about being able to access the backline, or some other vanguard-punch-through ability. Landed from the content editor 28 September: numbers, fixed component and loadout are the Mandrill's (the editor's template shape), the designation is Claude's fill in Minerva's register, and the passive is null because the editor's copy still carried the Mandrill's Subspace Solenoid and the note above says it is unwritten. All Ryan's to move.

design.fantasy: A fast, agile, and lightly armoured skirmisher, able to skim in and out of fights with ease. It's signature ability allows it to serve as both a potent scout and harasser before getting away with minimal damage.
design.name_clash: Flagged 28 September: Coyote is a Heavy Gear Peace River strider and a British reconnaissance vehicle. Another session is renaming it Prairie Dog the same afternoon; the note only keeps the build green until that lands.
design.notes: Landed from the content editor 28 September: numbers and fixed component are the Mandrill's (the editor's template shape), the loadout is the Mandrill's trimmed to four (the Heat Sink dropped) to fit the hardpoints, the designation is Claude's fill in Wainwright & Sutler's register, and the passive is planned until the engine can run it. All Ryan's to move.

passive.name: Coyote Howl
passive.description: Withdrawing from a skirmish occurs before the enemy takes their turn. This ability gains a 25% chance to fail for each additional ally in the skirmish.

design.fantasy: A small, nimble, lightly armoured vehicle designed to support heavy armour in combat. Able to stealthily avoid combat until its allies are in position for a flanking or pincer attack, then capitalize on openings in combat.
design.name_clash: Flagged 28 September: Dingo is a Heavy Gear Northern gear, and the Bundeswehr's four-wheeled armoured car. Kept for now so the build stays green; Ryan to rename or confirm.
design.notes: Landed from the content editor 28 September: numbers and fixed component are the Mandrill's (the editor's template shape), the loadout is the Mandrill's trimmed to four (the Heat Sink dropped) to fit the hardpoints, the designation is Claude's fill in Wainwright & Sutler's register, and the passive is planned until the engine can run it. All Ryan's to move.

passive.name: Adaptive Camouflage
passive.description: The Dingo is not forced into combat unless it intercepts a foe's path. Dingo attacks always deal max damage when in combat with at least one active ally.

design.fantasy: The larger cousin of the Sparrowhawk, trades explosiveness for longevity. Wide downturned wings evoking a hovering predator, weapon mounts mounted under the wings. Double boosters mounted on top of the tail section (similar to an A10 warthog).
design.notes: Locked weapon(s) should vent heat and deal increased damage proportional to heat vented. Landed from the content editor 28 September: numbers, fixed component and loadout are the Mandrill's (the editor's template shape), the designation is Claude's fill in Kestrel's register, and the passive is planned until the engine can run it. All Ryan's to move.
design.name_clash: Flagged 28 September: Goshawk is the Inner Sphere name of the Clan Vapor Eagle (a 55-ton 'Mech), and there is a Goshawk II. Kept for now so the build stays green; Ryan to rename or confirm.

passive.name: Thermal Recoupler
passive.description: Damage and shield recharge increases as heat approaches maximum.

design.fantasy: A hulking, neckless, spiked brute. Thick arms made for pummeling. A glowing firey core in its torso that lights up as the mech takes damage and heats up.
design.notes: One or more locked components should grant overheating, or deal self -damage. Landed from the content editor 28 September: numbers, fixed component and loadout are the Mandrill's (the editor's template shape), the designation is Claude's fill in the Arsenal's register, the sixth hardpoint takes a Chainsaw Claw (a melee stand-in until the Arsenal has weapons) because a shipped chassis fills every slot, and the passive is planned until the engine can run it. All Ryan's to move.

passive.name: Hellfire Capacitor
passive.description: Melee damage increases for each stack of Overheating. Taking damage gains 1 stack of Overheating.

design.fantasy: A sinister digitigrade figure, with 4 clawed arms, the middle set which can be used as an additional pair of legs. A low-set snout like cockpit with burning "eyes." Absorbs energy from units it defeats with its 4 signature locked claw weapons, granting permanent overcharge.
design.notes: Needs 4 locked components: melee weapons that grant overcharge on kill. Not sure of name, something sinister about assimilation or draining or attuning or something. Landed from the content editor 28 September: numbers and loadout are the Mandrill's (the editor's template shape) with nothing fixed and eight hardpoints as Ryan set them, three Chainsaw Claws stand in for the locked claws above because a shipped chassis fills every slot, the designation is Claude's fill in the Arsenal's register, and the passive is planned until the engine can run it. All Ryan's to move.

passive.name: Demonic Flywheel
passive.description: Overcharge on this unit does not decay, and persists between skirmishes.
